t: In front of you is the Raoul Wallenberg Monument, a ten-foot bronze figure standing outside the Western Marble Arch Synagogue, near the Swedish Embassy. Behind him is a bronze wall made up of a hundred thousand protective passes, the Schutzpässe he used to rescue Hungarian Jews. Wallenberg was a Swedish diplomat who, as special envoy in Budapest in 1944, issued protective passports and sheltered Jews in buildings he declared Swedish territory. The sculptor was Philip Jackson, a Royal Sculptor to Queen Elizabeth the Second.
